status: Locked exploratory pilot; historical ledger has already been inspected. No fresh holdout or novelty certification.
panel: Existing address-proxy panel; one address is an observational unit, not a proved unique cryptographic key.
start_source: data/replay/starts.csv, pre-existing quarterly pools with one draw
control_inventory: Bucket 0 only. Select up to 50000 addresses with positive control opening risk at onset; rank by total initial unspent above-dust balance, then stable anonymous ID. Selection may use only creation, unspent status, reveal status and balance at onset. No future-spend, future-survival, age-transition or future-linkage filters.
resource_budget: Charge the entire above-dust initial unspent balance of every activated control address, including initially immature outputs. This covers outputs that can enter the eligible cohort later within 364 days. New post-onset outputs cannot reach 365-day dormancy within the horizon. C is mobilisable initial value, not a burn, fee bill or net economic cost.
control_activation: At each week opening, in fixed onset rank order, activate a not-yet-used address only if its key is still unrevealed, it has eligible control value, and its charged initial balance fits the available cumulative resource allowance. Spend all its then-eligible initial outputs. Advance its reveal time and rebuild all linked eligible intervals/events. Each address activated at most once. No future natural events used to choose an activation.
theft_budget: Fixed weekly BTC pace m * median(reference count-control sigma in the 52 strictly preceding weeks), chosen at onset. Up to 1000 address proxies per week. Existing onset-only pool ranks and whole-address replay convention. Same theft trajectory for every control, detector, poison budget and refit mode.
controls: min(address value,0.1 BTC), fit-scaled kappa and working variance as previous pilot
calibration: 2014-01-06 to 2019-12-30; fitted-model endpoint exclusive, calibration endpoint inclusive as the paper. Seed 20261016, 400 training-only 8-week block bootstraps, target ARL 104. CTM uses same untrimmed z and c=104.
operating_points: Calibrated point plus descriptive matched historical natural-window budgets 0.25 and 0.50 over all 76 four-week-spaced starts. Select smallest feasible kappa in pre-fixed geomspace(0.25,128,101) union {1}; publish actual realised FAR and unattainable points. Select and hash operating points before attack outcomes. This is retrospective operating-curve comparison, not prospective type-I certification.
refits: Primary frozen run holds the model available at onset fixed for all 52 weeks. Separate stress test refits both theft and control contamination, 13-week anchors, 104-week lookback, 13-week gap. Use mode-specific honest natural curves and matched operating points. No fixed-hazard theorem claimed for contaminated refits.
pre_outcome_amendment: Before computing natural operating points or attack outcomes, replaced the initially described exogenous honest calendar refits with an onset-frozen model for the primary theorem run. This removes the need for a trusted unpoisoned future refit and implements the agreed fixed-hazard first step. Same starts, candidates, weights, budgets and attack policies.
outcomes: charged capital and actually moved value
paired_analysis: Average paired differences within start across the four fixed theft scenarios; circular moving-block bootstrap over the eight chronological starts, block length 2, 10000 resamples, seed 20261103. Exploratory interval only: few dependent starts, one target draw, history previously inspected. Also publish every paired outcome.
decision: Expand only if masking protection yields a useful loss/false-alarm tradeoff at shared attainable budgets, or a defensible new resource-constrained theorem. Do not infer detector superiority from predicted-flow shifts alone. No paper insertion at this stage.
known_scope_limits: address-proxy theft convention inherited from the existing replay
cross-address cryptographic linkage is not certified
new incoming transfers are held exogenous
fees and script signing are not measured
no full end-to-end loss theorem without a legitimate-behaviour model
